microgravity_evidence.flame_behavior_notes: Don noted significant vapor jetting. Flame not very long , but very sooty. Don set up a 2nd still camera taking pictures 1/s at F7, Aperture priority, spot metering on center of sphere in brackets of 3. Don noted equatorial division between 'charred' front like coating on meterorites, and matt black sooty rear hemispheres. Broke igniter. 2 minute burn.

microgravity_evidence.flame_behavior_notes: Very bright sooty ball. Lots of vapor jetting. N2 on at 1 minute. Blew off stagnation region but N2 did not extinguish wake, even with air flow off. Don turned off air, then N2 after some seconds. Wake flame sooty and wind-blown. Only extinguishes when all flow stops. N2 is entraining air to flame zone. Don noted that there was no soot on the sphere, just the 'char layer'. ~ 2 minute total burn.

findings.claim: In slow airflow a flame can spread upstream, into the incoming air, which is the opposite of what happens in normal gravity.
The flammability boundary for solids has a minimum oxygen limit at a gas speed of roughly 10 cm/s, which is also where flame spread is fastest, and that speed is typical of spacecraft ventilation.

investigations.title: Spacecraft Fire Experiment-II
investigations.objective: The objectives of SAFFIRE-II are to determine how rapidly a large scale fire grows in low-gravity and to investigate the low-g flammability limits compared to those obtained in NASA's normal gravity material flammability screening test.
investigations.hypothesis: This investigation hypothesizes that due to large differences between fire behavior in normal and reduced gravity, the use of terrestrial fires and fire standards to design spacecraft fire safety systems presents an inherent risk to the vehicle because of the significant level of uncertainty. While this approach has been successful thus far, the uncertainty and risk will increase as exploration missions venture further from earth with considerably longer transit times for a safe return. There is a significant lack of microgravity data available for spacecraft designers on which to base their fire safety designs and procedures. To address this knowledge gap, this investigation proposed to conduct large-scale fire safety experiments in an expendable spacecraft without risk to a crew.
